state:
Goal `core-request-mount-and-1-more`: `Core\Request\Mount` has every proof, and its check is green.
`Core\Request\Part` has its class card, and every member has its `covers:` markers on a Rust test and a `.nvst` case.
`content`, `name`, `readAll` and `saveTo` have every proof on disk and pass `bun nv proofs --verify`.
`filename` and `contentType` still owe examples, an attack, a bench and `about.md`. They are all that stands between the goal and `dossier-core-request-part`.
A proof program that needs a request does not run under `bun nv try`, and a loop of `nvs run` over the trees is refused by the guard: `bun nv proofs --run --id '<member>' --show` runs every example, attack and bench of one member and prints what each printed.
A request program has no capability at all. `saveTo`'s example and attack directories and `benches/members/core/Request-Part/` each carry an `nvs.toml` granting `fs` read and write, which every bench in that class directory now runs under.
`Core\Csv::parse` takes a plain `string`, so an upload cannot reach it even through `Core\Encoding::decodeText`. An example that parses an upload does not compile (see Backlog).

items.text: **`Core\Request\Part::filename`** — owes examples, hostile, perf, about.md (`rule:testing/feature-proofs`). The member is `crates/nvs-stdlib/src/request.rs:3406` and its card is `crates/nvs-stdlib/src/request.rs:1318`. `docs/examples/core/Request-Part/name/` is the shape. A quoted `filename` loses its backslashes when the form is read (`..\a` arrives as `..a`), and `tests/hostile/core/Request-Part/saveTo/01-a-save-that-lands-in-the-wrong-place.nvs` already sends a `../` name, so the attack takes another angle: a very long name, an empty one, a control character.

**`Core\Request\Part::contentType`** — owes examples, hostile, perf, about.md. The member is `crates/nvs-stdlib/src/request.rs:3414` and its card is `crates/nvs-stdlib/src/request.rs:1328`. `docs/examples/core/Request/files/03-checking-an-avatar-before-it-is-stored.nvs` already checks a type against a list. When both land, `dossier-core-request-part` should be green: run `bun nv proofs --verify --group 'Core\Request\Part'`, then close the goal per the loop's `DONE` step.

backlog: A second read of a part that was already read returns empty content from `readAll` and `content()`, and `saveTo` with `{overwrite: true}` then replaces a good copy with an empty file. `rule:http-server/a-part-is-consumed-in-one-of-three-ways` says a part is read "exactly once" but not what a second read does. A `LogicError` would be clearer. This is a design question for ADR 0105's owner, and no proof fails on it.

`Core\Csv::parse` (`crates/nvs-stdlib/src/csv.rs:210`) takes `CoreTy::Str`, so a `tainted string` from an upload cannot be parsed at all, while `rule:http-server/a-part-is-consumed-in-one-of-three-ways` names "a CSV about to be parsed" as what `readAll` is for. A taint-preserving parameter (tainted in, tainted rows out) is the likely fix; it is owed by whoever owns `Core\Csv`.
